_doc: Arc-length trim of arrowheaded stroke paths (ARROWTRIM). trim_path walks in from each armed end by the setback distance along arc length, de-Casteljau-splits the straddled segment, drops the tail, and butts the cut. Arc length uses the house FLATTEN_STEPS=20 uniform-t polyline (identical to flatten_path_commands / measure.arc_lengths / the dash-anchor walk), so the arc->parameter mapping is byte-reproducible across the active ports. Goldens are the trimmed command list pinned to the 4-decimal doc-space law. An empty result means the setbacks meet-or-exceed the total length: draw arrowheads only (oriented off the original path), no stroke. Vectors with orient=true instead pin the ARROWFIX2 head-orientation law (head_angles): the result is {start, end} head ANGLES in radians (null when that head is unarmed, i.e. its setback is 0). The head POSITION is unchanged (the original endpoint); the ANGLE is the chord over the head's own footprint from the trim CUT-POINT to the original endpoint (heads-only -> whole-path chord; wholly degenerate -> tangent walk), immune to end-hooks and sub-pixel final segments.

vectors.name: line_both_ends
vectors._comment: 100-long horizontal line, trim 10 off start and 20 off end -> M(10,0) L(80,0). Exact, hand-verifiable.

vectors.name: corner_span_two_segments
vectors._comment: Two 50-long legs; trim 10/10. Kept stroke spans the (50,0) corner joint.

vectors.name: cubic_end_trim
vectors._comment: Symmetric arch cubic; trim ~25% of arc off the end. Kept endpoint lands ON the curve (de Casteljau split), lifted off y=0, short of x=40 -- not the folded anchor the old shorten produced.

vectors.name: line_then_cubic_end_trim_stays_in_cubic
vectors._comment: Line leg then a cubic; a small end trim splits only the trailing cubic, the line and the joint survive whole.

vectors.name: overlapping_setbacks_heads_only
vectors._comment: 25 + 25 > 40 -> the two trims cross -> nothing remains (heads-only).

vectors.name: orient_jyh_pen_release_tail_s100
vectors._comment: JYH real pen-release tail (last two curves of Untitled-2.svg). The final ~1.3px segment has ctrl2 coincident with the endpoint. Triangle head (back 4.0), stroke width 6.6667, scale 100 -> end_setback = 4.0*6.6667 = 26.6668, which exceeds the 23.0559 tail length: heads-only, so the end head orients off the whole-tail chord (416.6667,174.6667)->(406,154.6667) = -2.0608 rad (up-and-left on screen), NOT the -2.5092 rad the old tangent-walk reads off the 1.05px ctrl1->endpoint scrap.

vectors.name: orient_jyh_pen_release_tail_s200
vectors._comment: Same real tail, triangle head scale 200 -> end_setback = 53.3336, still exceeds the 23.0559 tail -> heads-only -> identical whole-tail chord -2.0608 rad. Pins that the head is stable under scale even where the setback eats the whole tail.

vectors.name: orient_big_arch_end_s100
vectors._comment: A big symmetric arch (arc length 278.6285). Triangle head scale 100 -> end_setback 26.6668 cuts MID-PATH (non-degenerate), so the end head orients off the cut->endpoint chord = -1.3745 rad, shallower than the raw end tangent (straight down, -pi/2).

vectors.name: orient_big_arch_end_s200
vectors._comment: Same arch, triangle head scale 200 -> end_setback 53.3336: a larger head samples a longer, shallower chord = -1.1653 rad. Pins scale sensitivity of the chord law on a curved end.

vectors.name: orient_big_arch_both_ends_s100
vectors._comment: Arch with both heads armed at scale 100 (start_setback = end_setback = 26.6668, non-degenerate): start head chord = -1.7671 rad (outward), end head chord = -1.3745 rad (travel).

vectors.name: orient_start_hook_s100
vectors._comment: A ~1px start hook then a long +x leg. Triangle head scale 100 on the START (start_setback 26.6668, end unarmed). The start head orients off the chord straight back = PI (3.1416, outward), NOT the old tangent-walk's 2.3562 rad (135deg) read off the hook's first control point.
